newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar on Wednesday following the rise of the U.S. currency in overseas markets, dealers said.

"The dollar rose abroad and the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the local market to prevent the basket from falling by more than seven percent below the diagonal rate," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
"I believe that the central bank had to invest less than $100 million today," he said.
On Sunday a Treasury official said the bank had spent more than $1 billion during January intervening in the market.
"Overall volume was relatively low and investors showed little interest as they mourned the loss of life in the air crash," the dealer said.
Seventy-three Israeli soldiers were killed when two military helicopters heading for Lebanon crashed on Tuesday in the worst air disaster in Israeli military history.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3220 shekels against 3.3160 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6297 shekels against 3.6299 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6908 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7141 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0113 shekels against 2.0197 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3200 shekels.
